p: Which statement correctly compares the three YANG model families on IOS XE?
o: All three are written by Cisco, so they cover the same features under different names
IETF models are standards, OpenConfig is operator-led, and native models are Cisco's own
Native models are vendor-neutral, while IETF and OpenConfig models are specific to each vendor
OpenConfig models only hold operational data, so configuration must use IETF or native models
e: IETF and OpenConfig models are vendor-neutral, written by a standards body and an operator group respectively. Native models cover Cisco-specific features, and OpenConfig models include both configuration and state.

p: Which two statements about the NETCONF `<hello>` exchange are true? (Choose two.)
o: The server's hello includes the session-id for this session
Only the client sends a hello, and the server replies with `<ok/>`
The client's hello carries its first edit-config request for the server
Each side lists the capabilities it supports, such as base:1.1 and candidate
The client sends its username and password inside its hello
e: Both peers send a hello with their capabilities, and the server adds a session-id. Authentication happens in SSH before NETCONF starts, and operations follow the hello.

p: logging is added to system by an augment in the example-logging module (prefix exlog). Which JSON body is valid for PUT /restconf/data/example-system:system?
o: `{"example-system:system": {"hostname": "R1", "exlog:logging": {"level": "debug"}}}`
`{"example-system:system": {"hostname": "R1"}, "example-logging:logging": {"level": "debug"}}`
`{"example-system:system": {"hostname": "R1", "logging": {"level": "debug"}}}`
`{"example-system:system": {"hostname": "R1", "example-logging:logging": {"level": "debug"}}}`
e: A node from a different module than its parent is prefixed with that module's name, not its YANG prefix. Its children are in the same module, so level needs no prefix, and logging sits inside system.
c:
module: example-system
  +--rw system
     +--rw hostname?        string
     +--rw exlog:logging
        +--rw exlog:level?   enumeration

p: The module's namespace is urn:example:acl. Which XML sets the permitted hosts 10.1.1.1 and 10.1.1.2?
o: `<acl xmlns="urn:example:acl"><permitted-host list="10.1.1.1 10.1.1.2"/></acl>`
`<acl xmlns="urn:example:acl"><permitted-host>10.1.1.1</permitted-host><permitted-host>10.1.1.2</permitted-host></acl>`
`<acl xmlns="urn:example:acl"><permitted-host>10.1.1.1,10.1.1.2</permitted-host></acl>`
`<acl xmlns="urn:example:acl"><permitted-host><address>10.1.1.1</address><address>10.1.1.2</address></permitted-host></acl>`
e: Each leaf-list value is its own element named for the leaf-list. Values aren't joined, wrapped in child elements or written as attributes.

p: A POST creates tunnel 5 with only id and source, and the device rejects it. Why?
o: id must be sent as a string, because keys are always strings in JSON
source must be left out, because a POST may only contain key leaves
mode has no ? marker, so it's mandatory and must be included
mtu has no default value, so every optional leaf must be supplied too
e: In RFC 8340 trees, ? marks an optional node. A leaf without it, other than a key, is mandatory. Optional leaves can be left out.
c:
module: example-tunnel
  +--rw tunnels
     +--rw tunnel* [id]
        +--rw id        uint16
        +--rw mode      enumeration
        +--rw source?   string
        +--rw mtu?      uint16

p: Which two statements about this list are true? (Choose two.)
o: next-hop is optional, because only the first key in a list is mandatory
An entry is identified by prefix and next-hop together
In a RESTCONF URL, an entry is `route=<prefix>,<next-hop>`, with the prefix's slash percent-encoded
The entries are ordered by the user, because the list has two keys
Two entries can't share a prefix, because prefix is the first key
e: A list with several keys identifies entries by all of them, so two routes can share a prefix with different next hops. RESTCONF separates key values with commas, and every key is mandatory.
c:
module: example-routing
  +--rw static-routes
     +--rw route* [prefix next-hop]
        +--rw prefix      inet:ipv4-prefix
        +--rw next-hop    inet:ipv4-address
        +--rw distance?   uint8

p: A Netmiko script pushes interface changes to many switches. It must stop when a device rejects any line with % Invalid input. Which approach fits?
o: Call send_config_set(cmds, error_pattern=r"% Invalid"), which raises an exception on a match
Set fast_cli=False, which makes Netmiko stop on the first rejected line
Call send_command for each line, which raises an exception on any % message
Call send_config_set(cmds) and check whether it returned True, which it only does when every line is accepted
e: send_config_set returns the device output as a string. error_pattern makes Netmiko raise an exception when the output matches, so the script can stop.

p: The netops account logs in at user EXEC (Router>), and this fails with 'Failed to enter configuration mode'. What's the fix?
o: Add "secret" with the enable password to dev, and call conn.enable() before sending
Use send_command instead, which can configure from user EXEC mode
Add "configure terminal" as the first item in the command list
Change device_type to cisco_ios, which enters privileged mode automatically
e: Netmiko enters configuration mode from privileged EXEC, and enable() uses the secret to get there. send_config_set already sends configure terminal, and cisco_ios behaves the same way.
c:
dev = {"device_type": "cisco_xe", "host": "10.0.0.21",
       "username": "netops", "password": os.environ["SW_PASS"]}

with ConnectHandler(**dev) as conn:
    conn.send_config_set(["ntp server 10.0.0.123"])

p: Put these NETCONF steps for a safe change through the candidate datastore in order.
e: Locking first stops other sessions from changing the candidate during the edit, and validation checks the edited candidate before it's committed. The lock is released afterwards.

p: What does this call do?
o: It fails, because default_operation can only be merge on IOS XE
It merges the hostname, because replace is ignored on the running datastore
It replaces the whole running configuration with one that holds only a hostname
It changes only the hostname, because replace applies to the hostname leaf alone
e: default-operation replace makes the config element replace the target datastore, so everything not in it is removed. Use merge, or put operation="replace" on the one node to replace.

p: A script changes configuration over RESTCONF and must then save it to startup. Which request does that on IOS XE?
o: `PUT /restconf/data/startup-config` with the running configuration
`POST /restconf/operations/cisco-ia:save-config`
`PATCH /restconf/data/cisco-ia:save-config` with {"save": true}
`POST /restconf/data/Cisco-IOS-XE-native:native/write-memory`
e: RPCs are invoked with POST under /restconf/operations, and cisco-ia:save-config copies running to startup. RESTCONF has no startup datastore resource.

p: Which expression completes the function?
o: r.json()
r.json()["ietf-interfaces:interfaces-state"]["interface"]
r.json()["ietf-interfaces:interface"]
r.json()["interface"]
e: A GET on a list returns an object with one module-qualified member that holds the entries. The parent container isn't included, because the URL already points at the list.
c:
def down_interfaces(base, auth):
    # Purpose: list interfaces whose oper-status isn't up
    r = requests.get(f"{base}/data/ietf-interfaces:interfaces-state/interface",
                     auth=auth, verify="corp-ca.pem",
                     headers={"Accept": "application/yang-data+json"})
    return [i["name"] for i in ________ if i["oper-status"] != "up"]

p: Loopback1 and Loopback2 exist. A RESTCONF PATCH to /restconf/data/ietf-interfaces:interfaces sends a body containing only Loopback3. What's the result?
o: Only Loopback3 exists, because the body replaces the interface list
The request fails, because PATCH can't create new list entries
Loopback1 and Loopback2 are kept, and Loopback3 is ignored
All three loopbacks exist, because PATCH merges list entries
e: PATCH merges the body into the target, adding new entries and leaving the others alone. A PUT to the same URL would replace the list's contents.

p: Before a maintenance window, an engineer wants to see which lines a cisco.ios playbook would change on each switch, without changing anything. How?
o: Run ansible-playbook with --check --diff
Run ansible-playbook with --list-tasks
Run ansible-playbook with --syntax-check
Run ansible-playbook with -vvv against a single switch
e: Check mode makes no changes, and --diff shows the lines that would change for modules that support it. syntax-check and list-tasks never contact devices, and verbose output doesn't prevent changes.

p: Which cisco.ios.ios_config save_when value copies running to startup only when the two configurations differ?
o: never
always
modified
changed
e: modified compares running with startup and saves when they differ, even if this task changed nothing. changed saves only when this task made a change, always saves on every run, and never doesn't save.

p: A new switch with no configuration gets an address from this pool. What happens next?
o: It contacts Catalyst Center at 10.50.0.10 for PnP onboarding
It loads ztp.py as its startup configuration and reboots
It downloads ztp.py over HTTP and runs it in Guest Shell
It ignores the option, because ZTP only supports TFTP
e: Option 67 gives the ZTP script's location, and IOS XE accepts HTTP or TFTP URLs. The switch starts Guest Shell and runs the Python script there.
c:
ip dhcp pool ZTP-NEW
 network 10.50.0.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 10.50.0.1
 option 67 ascii http://10.50.0.10/ztp.py

p: Put the IOS XE ZTP steps in order.
e: ZTP only starts without a startup configuration, the DHCP reply supplies the script's location, and the script can only run once it's downloaded.
s: The switch downloads the script named in option 67
The switch boots and finds no startup configuration
Guest Shell runs the Python script, which configures the switch
The switch sends a DHCP request and gets an address with option 67

p: Which RESTCONF URL reads GigabitEthernet1/0/1 from the Cisco-IOS-XE-native model?
o: `/restconf/data/Cisco-IOS-XE-native:native/interface/GigabitEthernet=GigabitEthernet1%2F0%2F1`
`/restconf/data/Cisco-IOS-XE-native:native/interface/GigabitEthernet=1%2F0%2F1`
`/restconf/data/Cisco-IOS-XE-native:native/interface=GigabitEthernet1%2F0%2F1`
`/restconf/data/Cisco-IOS-XE-native:native/interface/GigabitEthernet=1/0/1`
e: The native model has a list for each interface type, keyed by the number alone, such as 1/0/1, and the slashes must be percent-encoded. The ietf-interfaces model uses the full name instead.

p: A script's lock on the candidate datastore returns this. What does it mean?
o: Session 42 already holds the lock, so wait for it to finish or end that session
The script's user lacks privilege 15, so the device refuses the lock
The script must unlock running before it can lock candidate
The candidate datastore isn't enabled on this device
e: lock-denied names the session that holds the lock in error-info. If that session is stale, an administrator can end it with kill-session. Missing rights give access-denied instead.

p: What makes this applet run?
o: GigabitEthernet0/0/2 going down
Any syslog message that contains the word ISP1
A timer that runs the applet every 10 seconds, whatever the state of the link
The tracked IP SLA probe to 203.0.113.1 changing to down
e: event track fires when the tracked object changes state. Here the object follows IP SLA 10, which pings 203.0.113.1 every 10 seconds.
c:
ip sla 10
 icmp-echo 203.0.113.1 source-interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0
 frequency 10
ip sla schedule 10 life forever start-time now
track 10 ip sla 10 reachability
!
event manager applet ISP1-DOWN
 event track 10 state down
 action 1.0 cli command "enable"
 action 2.0 cli command "configure terminal"
 action 3.0 cli command "interface GigabitEthernet0/0/2"
 action 4.0 cli command "no shutdown"
 action 5.0 syslog msg "ISP1 unreachable, backup link enabled"

p: guestshell enable fails on a Catalyst 9300. Which configuration must be in place first?
o: iox, which enables the application-hosting framework
netconf-yang, which starts the YANG agent that Guest Shell needs
ip http secure-server, which serves the Guest Shell image
event manager environment iox true, which lets EEM start containers
e: Guest Shell is an IOx application, so the IOx framework must be enabled with the iox command. NETCONF and the HTTPS server aren't required.

p: New switches haven't shipped yet. How can Catalyst Center be prepared so each one is provisioned as soon as it first connects?
o: Wait until they appear as Unclaimed, because PnP can't accept devices before they connect
Add their serial numbers to Plug and Play and claim them to sites ahead of time
Add them to inventory with the network-device API, using the IP addresses they'll get from DHCP
Create a discovery job for the branch subnets, which onboards factory-default switches
e: PnP accepts planned devices by serial number, with a site, image and template assigned. When a switch with that serial contacts Catalyst Center, it's provisioned straight away. Discovery needs devices that already have credentials.

p: A Meraki order has arrived. Which Dashboard API call adds all its devices and licenses to the organization's inventory by order number?
o: `POST /organizations/{organizationId}/claim` with orders
`POST /organizations/{organizationId}/devices` with serials
`POST /networks/{networkId}/devices/claim` with orders
`PUT /organizations/{organizationId}/inventory` with orders
e: The organization claim endpoint accepts orders, serials or licenses and adds them to inventory. Claiming into a network then assigns devices to that network.

p: A WAN edge site can't reach the Plug and Play Connect cloud. How can its router still onboard to SD-WAN Manager?
o: Point it at Catalyst Center, which forwards it to SD-WAN Manager
Configure it with the full CLI configuration by hand, which SD-WAN Manager then adopts automatically
It can't; every SD-WAN edge must reach Plug and Play Connect to onboard
Generate a bootstrap configuration file in SD-WAN Manager and load it from USB or bootflash
e: A bootstrap file carries the Validator address, organization name and certificate details, so the router can join without the cloud redirect. Catalyst Center doesn't onboard SD-WAN edges.

p: Put the steps of a Catalyst Center script that assigns a device to a site in order.
e: Every call needs the token, the assignment needs the siteId, and the task only exists once the POST returns it.
s: GET the site by name to find its siteId
Poll the task until it finishes, and check isError
POST the assignment and read the taskId from the response

p: Which SDK method completes this call to configure port 12 on the switch?
o: switch.updateDeviceSwitchPort
switch.createDeviceSwitchPortConfig
devices.updateDevice
networks.updateNetworkSwitchPort
e: SDK methods follow the API's scope and operation. Switch ports belong to a device, identified by serial, and are changed with updateDeviceSwitchPort.

p: A script attaches a device template through SD-WAN Manager and gets back an id. What should it do next?
o: Reboot the edge, because templates only take effect after a reload
Poll GET /dataservice/device/action/status/{id} until the push finishes
Nothing, because the template is in place once the POST returns
Call GET /dataservice/client/token with the id to confirm the push
e: Template attachment runs as an asynchronous action, and the action status endpoint reports progress and errors for each device.

p: Catalyst Center manages 1,200 devices, but GET /dna/intent/api/v1/network-device returns only 500. What's the fix?
o: Call the API again, because the first call only returns cached results
Get a new token, because each token is limited to 500 results until it's refreshed
Add ?all=true to the URL to remove the maximum
Request further pages with offset and limit until fewer than limit come back
e: The API returns a page at a time, with limit capped at 500 and offset starting at 1. Loop over the pages until a short page arrives.

p: What does this render for the interface?
o: switchport access vlan, with an empty VLAN number
switchport mode trunk and switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20
Both the trunk lines and shutdown
shutdown, because port.vlan isn't defined
e: The first condition is false, and the elif is true because mode is trunk and vlans exists, so only that branch renders.

p: What does this render?
o: switchport trunk allowed vlan 10 20 30
switchport trunk allowed vlan ,10,20,30
switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30,
switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30
e: loop.last is true only on the final item, so a comma follows every value except the last. An inline if renders nothing when its condition is false.
c:
{# vlans = [10, 20, 30] #}
switchport trunk allowed vlan {% for v in vlans %}{{ v }}{{ "," if not loop.last }}{% endfor %}

p: Why does this template use namespace() for the counter?
o: namespace() resets the counter at the start of each loop iteration
Jinja2 can't do arithmetic on a variable unless it's stored in a namespace object first
namespace() makes the counter global across every template that's rendered
Variables set inside a loop don't persist after it, but namespace attributes do
e: Loops have their own scope, so a plain set inside the loop is lost when it ends. Changing an attribute of a namespace object carries the value out.

p: Which two are advantages of the cisco.dnac Ansible collection over raw uri tasks against Catalyst Center? (Choose two.)
o: It removes the need for any credentials
It runs on the switches, so no control node is needed
It works even when the Catalyst Center API isn't reachable
It waits for asynchronous tasks and reports their result
It handles authentication and token reuse for each module
e: The modules wrap the API, including login and task polling, so playbooks stay short and idempotent. They still run on the control node and need API access and credentials.

p: Which expression completes the id line?
o: loop.id
item.id
vlans[item].id
vlans.id
e: Inside a loop, the current element is available as item, so its fields are item.id, item.name and so on.
c:
- name: Create branch VLANs
  cisco.meraki.networks_appliance_vlans:
    meraki_api_key: "{{ vault_meraki_key }}"
    networkId: "{{ net_id }}"
    id: "{{ ________ }}"
    name: "{{ item.name }}"
    subnet: "{{ item.subnet }}"
    applianceIp: "{{ item.gw }}"
    state: present
  loop: "{{ vlans }}"

p: A play with hosts: switches (40 switches) uses ansible.builtin.uri to create one Catalyst Center site, and it sends 40 identical API calls. What's the fix?
o: Run the task against localhost, or add run_once: true
Use connection: network_cli, so the API is called only once
Add serial: 1, so the switches call the API one at a time
Set gather_facts: false, which stops the repeated calls
e: A task runs once for each host in the play. Controller API calls belong in a play for localhost, or run_once makes the task run for only one host.

p: Policy requires blocking peer-to-peer traffic at every branch MX. Which Dashboard API call applies this to a network?
o: `PUT /networks/{networkId}/wireless/ssids/{number}` with peer-to-peer blocking turned on for each SSID
`PUT /networks/{networkId}/appliance/vlans` with the peer-to-peer VLAN removed
`PUT /networks/{networkId}/appliance/firewall/l7FirewallRules` with a category deny rule
`POST /networks/{networkId}/appliance/trafficShaping/rules` with a low priority
e: Layer 7 firewall rules can deny application categories such as peer-to-peer. Traffic shaping only limits bandwidth, and SSID settings don't cover wired clients behind the MX.

p: A new security group for contractors must be created in ISE through the API. Which request fits?
o: `POST /ers/config/networkdevicegroup` with the SGT value
`POST /ers/config/sgt` with a name and value
`POST /ers/config/endpointgroup` with the group name
`PUT /ers/config/ancpolicy` with the group name
e: Security groups are SGT objects in ERS. Endpoint identity groups, ANC policies and network device groups are different objects.

p: Security must find which network devices are affected by published Cisco security advisories. Which Catalyst Center API fits?
o: `GET /dna/intent/api/v1/site-health` with security filters
`GET /dna/intent/api/v1/event/subscription` for advisory events
`GET /dna/intent/api/v1/security-advisory/advisory`, then each advisory's device list
`GET /dna/intent/api/v1/network-device` with softwareVersion filters
e: The security advisories API matches device software against Cisco PSIRT advisories and lists the affected devices for each. Filtering by version by hand misses that matching logic.

p: ISE ERS returns 401 for every call, although the same account logs in to the ISE GUI. What's the most likely cause?
o: The script must call a token endpoint first and send X-Auth-Token
The account isn't in the ERS Admin or ERS Operator group
ERS is disabled, which makes ISE return 401 instead of refusing the connection
The request is missing a Content-Type header
e: ERS only accepts accounts in the ERS Admin or ERS Operator groups. ERS uses Basic authentication, and when the ERS service is disabled nothing listens on port 9060.

p: A Catalyst Center POST returns 202 with a taskId, and the task later shows isError: true. Where does the script find out why?
o: In the 202 response headers
Only in the Catalyst Center GUI, because the API doesn't expose task errors
In the task's failureReason and progress fields
In the device's syslog
e: The task object reports progress, isError and failureReason, which explain what went wrong. The 202 only confirms that the request was accepted.

p: After a change, a team wants Catalyst Center to confirm that traffic from a user subnet still reaches a server along the expected path. Which API fits?
o: `POST /dna/intent/api/v1/flow-analysis`, then read the path trace result
`GET /dna/intent/api/v1/network-device` for both endpoints
`POST /dna/intent/api/v1/network-device-poller/cli/read-request` with a ping
`GET /dna/intent/api/v1/site-health` for the user's site
e: Path Trace (flow-analysis) computes the hop-by-hop path between a source and a destination, including ACLs along the way. Device lists and health scores don't show the path.

p: Which pyATS feature lets a team write test steps, such as configure, execute and parse with checks, in YAML instead of Python?
o: Blitz
Unicon
Easypy
Clean
e: Blitz runs actions and checks defined in YAML. Unicon handles device connections, Clean prepares devices (for example, by loading images), and Easypy runs jobs.

p: Which two are good uses of a Cisco Modeling Labs topology in enterprise operations? (Choose two.)
o: Running automated tests in a CI pipeline before changes are deployed
Replacing monitoring of the production network
Rehearsing a routing migration with copies of the production configurations
Testing PoE power budgets on access switches
Measuring the line-rate throughput that the production switch hardware can forward
e: Virtual nodes run real network OS software, so they suit configuration, protocol and automation testing. They don't model hardware forwarding performance or physical features such as PoE.

p: How should production configurations be loaded onto CML nodes so they boot with them?
o: Copy the configurations to the CML server's disk, which every node reads at boot
Set each node's configuration in the lab topology or through the API before starting it
Push them over SSH from the production devices, which CML links to automatically
Start the nodes empty, because CML can't load configurations
e: Each node has a configuration that's applied when it boots, set in the topology YAML or with virl2_client. Changing it after boot means a wipe and restart, or pushing configuration as with any device.

p: Before activating a new image through Catalyst Center SWIM, which step confirms that devices have enough flash space and meet the other upgrade prerequisites?
o: The image update readiness check
Path Trace
A compliance check of the startup configuration
Marking the image golden
e: The readiness check verifies items such as flash space, the config register and service entitlement before distribution and activation. Marking an image golden only sets the standard version.

p: A Meraki firmware upgrade causes problems at one network. Which API call returns it to the previous version?
o: `DELETE /networks/{networkId}/firmwareUpgrades`
`POST /networks/{networkId}/firmwareUpgrades/rollbacks`
`PUT /devices/{serial}` with the old firmware version
`POST /devices/{serial}/reboot` on each affected device
e: The rollbacks endpoint schedules a return to the previous version for a product. Firmware isn't set per device, and a reboot doesn't change the version.

p: A NOC dashboard needs every Meraki device in the organization marked online, offline, alerting or dormant. Which call fits?
o: `GET /networks/{networkId}/events`
`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/apiRequests`
`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/devices/statuses`
`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/inventory/devices`
e: devices/statuses returns each device's current status. Inventory lists what's owned, events are a network's log, and apiRequests logs API use.

p: An on-call script must fetch active P1 issues from Catalyst Center Assurance. Which API fits?
o: `GET /dna/intent/api/v1/issues` with priority=P1
`GET /dna/intent/api/v1/network-device` with reachabilityStatus=P1
`GET /dna/intent/api/v1/task` with isError=true
`GET /dna/intent/api/v1/site-health` with priority=P1
e: The issues API returns Assurance issues and filters on priority and status. Tasks track API jobs, and the other endpoints don't hold issues.

p: This RPC is sent over a NETCONF session. How often does data arrive, and how long does the subscription last?
o: Every 6,000 seconds, until the device reloads
Every 6 seconds, until the NETCONF session closes
Every 60 seconds, permanently, because it's saved in the running configuration
Every 60 seconds, until the NETCONF session closes
e: period is in centiseconds, so 6000 is 60 seconds. establish-subscription creates a dynamic subscription, which ends with its session.

p: A configured subscription sends data to a Telegraf collector with protocol grpc-tcp. Which encoding must it use?
o: encode-gpb-compact
encode-json
encode-xml
encode-kvgpb
e: gRPC dial-out on IOS XE uses key-value Google Protocol Buffers. XML encoding is used for NETCONF dynamic subscriptions.

p: Which Catalyst Center API registers a set of events to be sent to an existing REST webhook destination?
o: `POST /dna/intent/api/v1/event/webhook`
`GET /dna/intent/api/v1/events`
`POST /dna/intent/api/v1/dna-event/notify`
`POST /dna/intent/api/v1/event/subscription/rest`
e: A REST event subscription ties event IDs to a webhook destination. /event/webhook creates the destination itself, and /events lists the event catalog.

p: Which two protect a webhook receiver that accepts alerts from a controller? (Choose two.)
o: Use HTTPS with a certificate the controller trusts
Check a shared secret or signature in each request
Accept any JSON body, so that no alerts are lost
Put the controller's API key in the receiver URL
Use plain HTTP, so the controller never hits certificate errors
e: HTTPS protects the payload in transit, and a shared secret or signature proves who sent it. Accepting anything invites forged alerts, and API keys don't belong in URLs.

p: What does AI-enhanced Radio Resource Management in Catalyst Center do?
o: It moves every wireless client to 6 GHz automatically
It replaces access point radios with software-defined radios
It uses cloud ML on RF data to recommend or apply channel and power changes
It turns off RF telemetry, because the AI predicts conditions instead
e: AI-enhanced RRM analyzes RF telemetry over time in the cloud and makes channel, power and width decisions. It still relies on telemetry from the access points.

p: How do AI features in controllers typically handle actions that would change the network?
o: They give recommendations or guided workflows that an admin reviews and approves
They send changes to the vendor for approval before applying them
They apply every change immediately, so that problems are fixed before anyone notices
They can only describe data and are never linked to any action
e: Controller AI usually suggests a fix or prepares a workflow, and a person decides. That keeps change control and accountability in place.

p: Which prompt is most likely to get accurate AI-generated code for a RESTCONF task?
o: "Write a RESTCONF script", then accept the first answer that runs
"Write a script to configure my switches."
"You're a world-class network engineer. Write the best possible automation script for my network, with no mistakes."
Give the IOS XE release, the YANG tree, a sample reply and the library to use, and ask for error handling
e: Specific context, such as the release, schema, sample data and libraries, grounds the model in your real environment. Vague prompts and pressure to be correct don't.

p: Which two practices make AI-assisted code development safer? (Choose two.)
o: Keep generated code in version control and review it in pull requests
Turn off the linter warnings that generated code triggers
Skip tests for generated code that already runs
Run linters and automated tests in CI on generated code
Let the assistant commit straight to the main branch
e: Generated code should go through the same review and testing as any other code. Skipping either lets errors reach production.

p: An AI agent only needs to read Meraki client lists, but it uses an organization-wide API key belonging to a full admin. What's the main risk, and the fix?
o: No risk, because API keys can only read data
Rate limits; give the agent several admin keys to spread the load
Slow responses; use a faster model so the key is used less often
Excessive permissions; use a key from a read-only account scoped to what it needs
e: If the agent is tricked or wrong, it can do anything the key allows, and Meraki API keys carry the full rights of their account. Least privilege limits the damage.

p: An agent turns user requests into CLI commands and runs them on switches. Which two controls reduce the risk? (Choose two.)
o: Require human approval for configuration changes, after showing a diff
Run whatever the model returns, since it was told to be careful
Leave the generated commands out of the logs to protect privacy
Check generated commands against an allow-list before running them
Give the agent enable access on every device, so that it never fails for missing rights
e: Model output can include unexpected or injected commands. Validate it, keep a person in the loop for changes, and keep audit logs.

p: What does this register?
o: A resource that holds the interface's current status
A system prompt that the server forces into every conversation
A reusable prompt template, with device and interface as arguments
A tool that the model calls to troubleshoot the interface
e: Prompts are message templates with arguments that the user picks. Tools perform actions, and resources provide data.

p: How can a FastMCP tool tell the model what each argument means?
o: Name each parameter in capital letters so the model notices it
Add the descriptions to the server's name, such as FastMCP("vlan tool: site=site code")
It can't; arguments have no descriptions, and only the docstring is sent
Annotate each parameter, such as Annotated[str, Field(description="Switch hostname")]
e: FastMCP builds the input schema from type hints, and Pydantic Field descriptions become part of that schema. The docstring describes the tool as a whole.

p: What does this script do?
o: It lists the server's tools without calling any of them
It starts the server over HTTP on port 8000 and waits for remote agents to connect
It connects to the server in memory and calls get_vlans directly, which suits tests
It asks an AI model to decide whether to call get_vlans
e: Passing the server object to Client uses an in-memory transport, so tools can be tested without a model or a network. In a real agent, the model decides which tools to call.
c:
import asyncio
from fastmcp import Client
from server import mcp

async def main():
    # Purpose: call a tool on the server without an AI model
    async with Client(mcp) as client:
        result = await client.call_tool("get_vlans", {"site": "akl"})
        print(result)

asyncio.run(main())
